issues.detail: Error handling is thin beyond the 429 rate-limit note: there are no troubleshooting steps for failed external data source connections, a lost JWT secret, 401/403 token errors, or webhook delivery failures.

scenarios.name: selfhost-postgres-metadata-stable-jwt
scenarios.rationale: Both give the pg:// NC_DB, port 8080 and a fixed NC_AUTH_JWT_SECRET with an explanation, and both advise pinning the tag. B follows the rubric more closely: it mounts at /usr/app/data/ with the trailing slash and loads the secret from an environment variable. A uses a named volume, hardcodes a placeholder secret, and puts the pin advice only in the notes, though it adds useful extras like URL-encoding and the SSL option.

scenarios.name: v3-api-query-and-create-records
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: v3 endpoint, xc-token header, URL-encoded where/sort/pageSize, a "fields" body, and the token from an environment variable. A uses the v2 endpoint with limit/offset and has no "fields" wrapper, so it misses most of the rubric.

scenarios.name: public-form-to-slack-webhook
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: table with Status, Form view with sharing, After insert webhook to Slack, and a v3 records query using where=(Status,eq,New) plus a public-link caution. B covers the table, form and webhook but verifies with a v2 query that has no Status filter, and it leaves out the Priority field.
